tasks.short: Observe milling operation and adjust controls for specified tolerances

steps.what: Observe actual milling or planing operation and compare workpiece results with the specified tolerances
inputs: Actual operation and workpiece
Job tolerances
Existing machine indications, defined as OTHER
outputs: Observed operating condition and conformity concerns

steps.what: Determine and check the exact control adjustment against the current job, machine condition and established procedure
inputs: Observed condition from s1
Actual machine controls and established job instructions
outputs: Human-selected and checked next adjustment or decision to stop

steps.what: Apply the exact checked adjustment using the machine controls and return to observation
inputs: Exact adjustment checked in s2
outputs: Actual changed control state for subsequent observation

tasks.design: Retain actual observation and human control decisions using the existing {OTHER} machine interface. Each control change follows the operator's check of that exact adjustment; no new machine-control mechanism is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task depends on actual cutting behaviour and workpiece condition.
tasks.enabler_now: No new software capability is established here that removes active observation or control work.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise changing conditions and assess whether adjustments achieve the required tolerances.
tasks.human_edge: Apply shop knowledge to the actual operation and stop when conditions are uncertain.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: observing machining and adjusting existing controls requires attention to the actual job; existing machine control does not itself establish a new labour saving.

assumptions: Illustrative active-effort split, not measured baseline or unattended machine runtime. Observation, control decision and actual actuation are separated before assigning zero saving.
Repeat s1 and s2 before each s3 adjustment; a changed value, workpiece or condition invalidates the previous check. This is ordinary operating judgement, not an added approval ceremony.
No distinct record write, report, send or lookup is established by this task statement. Do not add paperwork or claim a saving for automatic machine operation already present today.
No proposed change, so incremental work is explicitly zero. All 100 focal effort points remain; gross and net saving are zero.
unknowns: Actual machine controls and current monitoring arrangement
research_questions: Is any separate manual information transfer observed in this task?

already_counted.description: Ordinary selection and final checking of the actual adjustment

incremental.description: No new process or software to maintain

approvals.approved_version: Exact next adjustment checked in s2 for the actual current job and conditions; changes require a fresh check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All observation, judgement and actual control actions remain; no supported new mechanism removes labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and install cutting tools and accessories

steps.what: Find the current job specifications and existing tool and accessory information
inputs: Approved job specifications
Existing shop tool catalogue, defined as OTHER
outputs: Current specifications and candidate tool information

steps.what: Select the actual cutting tools and accessories and check the exact installation against specifications and current machine readiness
inputs: Specifications and catalogue information from s1
Actual tools, accessories and machine
outputs: Selected tools and checked installation readiness

steps.what: Install the selected cutting tools and accessories using the established hand-tool or power-tool procedure
inputs: Exact checked tool selection and readiness from s2
Actual hand tools or power tools
outputs: Installed cutting tools and accessories with actual fit checked

tasks.design: Configure native filters or bookmarks in the existing {OTHER} tool catalogue and {DOCS} job records. The operator selects, checks and physically installs the actual tools; the lookup does not choose or install them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current specifications and tool information can take repeated navigation to find.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing catalogue filters can expose the relevant records with their current version.
tasks.still_hard: Compatibility, condition and correct physical installation depend on the actual equipment.
tasks.human_edge: Select suitable tools and judge the actual fit and readiness.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native catalogue filtering can reduce navigation while physical tool selection and installation remain human work.

assumptions: Conditional episode with actual manual catalogue navigation, not a measured baseline. Source owners already maintain job specifications and the tool catalogue; operator retrieval and version checking remain in s1.
Native features first; existing equivalent filters earn no new saving. Ambiguous identifiers remain manual, with no generated substitution advice.

The ordinary readiness check in s2 covers the actual final tool choice before installation; changed tools or conditions require another check. No generated installation method or new physical automation.
No separate tool transaction, report or message is established; do not invent one. Overlapping specification lookup with 14004 is counted once when it is the same action.
All 100 illustrative focal effort points are independent of prompt time-share priors. Gross lookup saving 2 less upkeep 0.5 gives net 1.5.
unknowns: Current catalogue coverage and actual navigation effort
research_questions: Can current native filters remove repeated navigation without changing tool-selection judgement?

already_counted.description: Source lookup and exact tool and installation readiness judgement

incremental.description: Maintain catalogue filter and source links

approvals.approved_version: Exact tool and accessory choice checked against current specifications and readiness in s2; changes require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional native lookup saving 2 minus upkeep 0.5; physical installation and tool judgement retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Study job documents and determine tooling, materials and operation sequence

steps.what: Retrieve the correct current blueprints, layouts, sketches and work orders for the workpiece
inputs: Job identifier
Released drawings and work orders maintained in the shop job system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Current source documents with matching job and revision

steps.what: Study the actual drawings and orders to assess workpiece specifications, geometry and constraints
inputs: Current documents from s1
outputs: Operator's understanding of actual specifications and unresolved ambiguities

steps.what: Determine tooling instructions, needed tools and materials and the operation sequence, resolving unclear requirements with the responsible job owner
inputs: Actual specifications assessed in s2
Shop knowledge and owner clarification where needed
outputs: Human-determined tooling and material requirements and operation sequence

tasks.design: Use native job and revision filters in {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS} to retrieve the existing released documents. The operator still reads the drawings and determines tooling, materials and sequence from the actual job.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the correct revision can require repeated navigation between job records and drawings.
tasks.enabler_now: Native job links and exact revision filters can reduce document retrieval effort.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting geometry and planning feasible operations requires shop judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the workpiece and identify requirements needing clarification.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: controlled document systems can filter released drawings by exact job and revision; reading and process planning remain distinct human work.

assumptions: Conditional manual-navigation episode; no measured baseline or automatic drawing interpretation. Engineering and job owners already produce released documents; operator retrieval and revision checking are counted in s1.
Use native links first and stop on mismatched, missing or superseded sources. Existing links earn no new saving.

This task determines requirements and sequence; it does not establish a separate record write, release or machine command. Actual tooling installation and control changes are separate tasks with their own checks.

If a controlled instruction document must actually be authored and released, include its writing, final review and gated release before claiming a saving for that episode; none is silently eliminated here.
Deduplicate identical lookup actions with 14011. All 100 illustrative focal points: gross 4.5 less upkeep 1 gives net 3.5.
unknowns: Actual drawing access and instruction-authoring boundary
research_questions: Which document navigation is still manual and which job instructions are already released?

incremental.description: Maintain exact job and revision links

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Illustrative retrieval saving 4.5 minus upkeep 1; actual drawing study and process planning remain fully retained.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select cutting speeds, feed rates and depths of cut

steps.what: Identify actual workpiece material, tooling, machine constraints and the applicable established shop calculation references
inputs: Actual job, material and tool specifications
Established shop calculation reference and calculator, defined as OTHER
outputs: Checked input values, units and explicitly applicable formulas

steps.what: Perform exact shop-mathematics calculations from the operator's checked inputs and selected established formulas
inputs: Checked values, units and formulas from s1
outputs: Traceable arithmetic results and explicit input or unit errors

steps.what: Apply knowledge of metal properties and current conditions to select and check cutting speeds, feed rates and depths of cuts
inputs: Arithmetic results and original input references
Actual machine, tooling and workpiece conditions
outputs: Operator-selected parameters with unresolved cases held for clarification

tasks.design: Use existing {SPREADSHEET} formulas for explicit arithmetic after the operator checks inputs and selects the established calculation method. The operator determines all cutting parameters; this calculation does not write machine settings.
tasks.previous_blocker: Where arithmetic is still performed by hand, repeated calculation and unit handling consume active effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formulas can reproduce established calculations and flag explicit unit or missing-input errors.
tasks.still_hard: Material behaviour and actual equipment conditions require judgement beyond arithmetic.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether a calculation applies and choose parameters appropriate to the actual job.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: spreadsheet formulas can perform explicit arithmetic from checked inputs, while applicability and machining parameter selection remain operator judgements.

assumptions: Conditional episode where the operator actually performs these calculations manually; no measured baseline. If a native machining calculator already does them, s2 is baseline and incremental saving is zero.

Operator identifies and captures actual inputs, units and applicable established formulas in s1; no clean structured feed or newly generated machining method is assumed. Missing data and ambiguous applicability stop automated calculation.
Native calculator or spreadsheet configuration first; existing software runtime earns no saving. s2 replaces only actual manual arithmetic, not parameter selection.

This task selects parameters, with no separate saved record or machine command established. Applying any selected value requires the exact final-value and current-condition check before the separate control action in 14002; no hidden device write.
No numeric settings or new cutting procedures are supplied. All 100 illustrative focal effort points: gross 25 less upkeep 3 gives net 22.
unknowns: Existing calculator coverage and actual manual arithmetic effort
research_questions: Which calculations are still manual after current machine and shop software capabilities?

already_counted.description: Actual input and formula checking and final human parameter selection

incremental.description: Validate and maintain explicit calculation formulas and unit checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional manual arithmetic saving 25 minus upkeep 3; zero where existing tools already perform the calculation.
